summary: For visitors who do not need a visa for Singapore, the length of stay is set by the immigration officer at entry and sent as an e-Pass — up to 90 days for US and South Korean citizens and 30 days for holders of ordinary Chinese passports under the exemption in force since 9 February 2024 — but every visitor entering Singapore must submit the free SG Arrival Card (SGAC) online within 3 days before arrival.

conditionalWaivers.text: Nationals of India, and holders of a PRC Travel Document, a Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity or a Macao SAR Travel Permit (not ordinary Chinese passports), may be eligible for Singapore's 96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility when travelling to or from a third country, with an onward air, ferry or cruise ticket departing within 96 hours and a valid visa or long-term pass (valid at least one month from entry) for Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United Kingdom or the United States. Nationals of the CIS states (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan), Georgia, Turkmenistan and Ukraine need only an onward air ticket departing within 96 hours, and must leave by air. Transit only, and extension of stay is not allowed.

source.name: ICA — Visa-Free Transit Facility

fee.notes: A S$30 non-refundable processing fee, paid online by Visa or MasterCard card. Applications are submitted through a strategic partner or a local contact in Singapore, or at a Singapore Overseas Mission or its authorised visa agent.

notes: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned: it is illegal to bring them into Singapore, including for personal use, and those found with them have them confiscated and could be fined.

Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free concession for cigarettes and tobacco products: all of them, including packs bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST when brought in, and packs that do not meet Singapore's standardised-packaging rules are disposed of at the checkpoint.
Australia's Smartraveller says you may not bring in any chewing gum, including nicotine gum, even if you stay within the airport transit zone.
Australia's Smartraveller says penalties for drug offences include caning and the mandatory death sentence for some trafficking offences.

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are available across the country and hotels, restaurants and shops accept international credit cards, but hawker centres and small retailers may not, so cash may be required there.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says violent crime and theft are rare in Singapore. Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences elsewhere, including littering and jaywalking.

tips.text: ICA says submitting the SG Arrival Card is free and that commercial services charging a fee to submit it are not affiliated with ICA. Submit it at eservices.ica.gov.sg or via the MyICA app, within 3 days (including the day of arrival) before you arrive.
The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore: bringing them in is illegal even for personal use, and they are confiscated, with a possible fine.

Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free allowance for cigarettes or tobacco: every pack you bring in, even one bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, is subject to duty and GST, so declare it on arrival.

Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences elsewhere, including smoking in public, spitting, importing or chewing gum, littering and jaywalking, and that drug trafficking can carry the mandatory death sentence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Singapore?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free: the US State Department says no visa is required for 90 days or less, and the exact stay is set by the ICA officer at entry. You must also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival at eservices.ica.gov.sg.

faq.question: What is the SG Arrival Card and who needs it?
faq.answer: The SG Arrival Card (SGAC) is Singapore's free digital arrival declaration, including a health declaration. Every foreign visitor must submit it online within 3 days before arriving, via eservices.ica.gov.sg or the MyICA app. It is not a visa — visa-required nationals need both a visa and the SGAC.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit Singapore without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Since February 9, 2024, holders of ordinary passports issued by the People's Republic of China can stay in Singapore visa-free for up to 30 days. The SG Arrival Card is still required before arrival.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Singapore?
faq.answer: Yes. Indian passport holders need an entry visa before travelling, with a non-refundable S$30 processing fee. Applications are submitted online through a strategic partner or a local contact in Singapore, or at a Singapore mission or its authorised visa agent, and are processed within three working days. The SG Arrival Card must also be submitted before arrival.

faq.question: Can I bring cigarettes or a vape into Singapore?
faq.answer: Vapes and e-cigarettes: no — the UK government says they are banned and illegal to bring in, even for personal use. Cigarettes: yes, but Singapore Customs says there is no duty-free allowance for them — all cigarettes and tobacco products, even packs bought in Singapore with the duty-paid (SDPC) mark, are subject to duty and GST, so declare them on arrival.
